whatItDoes: Calculates your Body Mass Index (BMI) from your height and weight in either metric (cm/kg) or imperial (in/lb) units. Returns the BMI value to one decimal place, classifies it on the WHO standard scale (underweight, normal, overweight, obese class I-III), shows the BMI Prime ratio, and computes the healthy weight range for your height.
whyItExists: BMI is the most widely-used screening tool for weight categories that may lead to health problems. While it's not a perfect measure (it doesn't distinguish between muscle and fat), it's a fast, free, accessible first-pass indicator that millions of people use daily to check whether they fall in a healthy range. The calculator handles both metric and imperial units, with cm/m auto-detection for height and full WHO classification with educational descriptions.
whoShouldUse: Adults who want a quick BMI check, healthcare students learning the WHO classification, fitness coaches screening clients, parents checking their teenager's weight category, and anyone tracking weight as part of a health goal.

bestPractices: BMI is a population-level screening tool, not a personal health diagnosis
For children and teens (under 20), use the age- and sex-specific CDC BMI percentile instead of the standard adult cutoffs
Muscle weighs more than fat — athletes and bodybuilders often score 'overweight' or 'obese' despite being healthy
Pregnancy changes the meaning of BMI; consult a healthcare provider for prenatal weight guidance
Re-measure at the same time of day, ideally fasted, for consistent tracking
commonMistakes: Confusing the metric and imperial inputs (cm vs m, kg vs lb)
Treating BMI as a body-fat measurement — it isn't; it just uses weight
Using BMI as the only health metric — blood pressure, cholesterol, and lifestyle matter more
Believing the 'overweight' cutoff is wrong because you're muscular
Comparing adult and pediatric BMI without adjusting for age and sex
faq: What is BMI? Body Mass Index is a simple weight-to-height ratio (weight ÷ height²). It estimates body fat for most adults but is a screening tool, not a diagnosis.
Is the WHO classification accurate? For population screening yes, but it doesn't account for muscle mass, bone density, or ethnicity. Athletes routinely score 'overweight' or 'obese'.
What is BMI Prime? It's a simpler ratio: actual BMI ÷ 25 (the upper normal). 1.0 = upper normal, 1.5 = 50% over the upper normal. Clinicians find it easier to read.
Should I use metric or imperial? Both produce identical results. Use whichever you measure in. Use the 'Swap units' button to convert without re-entering values.
Is the calculation done in my browser? Yes — your height and weight never leave your device, never touch a server, never get logged.
What is the healthy weight range? For any height, the healthy BMI is 18.5-24.9. The calculator shows the corresponding weight range automatically.
